decisions.reason: The client explicitly requests long-term retention of the wiring layout alongside the CAD files, adding a retention obligation to the wiring-plan deliverable.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

The newest updates look great. Seeing the plumbing, drain routing, bowl integration, and full structure take shape has made me even more enthusiastic about the direction of the project.

While thinking about the future, I keep considering the possibility of eventually placing the Matcha Mixer in a retail setting if we decide to open a shop. For that reason, I’d like us to begin considering food-service and health department requirements now, while the machine is still at the prototype stage.

As development continues, I’d like to keep the following points in mind:

Food-contact materials such as stainless steel, food-grade plastics, food-grade silicone, etc.
Ease of sanitation and cleaning
Avoiding concealed spaces where liquid could collect or become trapped
Simple removal of the bowls, whisks, and other parts for cleaning
Keeping liquids separated from electrical components
Access for maintenance and servicing if a component ever requires replacement

When you have time, I’d also like to learn which materials are used wherever food contact occurs and whether you anticipate any areas presenting cleaning or sanitation difficulties.

Over the long term, I think retaining documentation for the following would be useful:

materials used
CAD files
wiring layout
cleaning procedures
exploded-view drawings if available

We don’t need all of that immediately, but if this develops into a larger project, that information could be extremely valuable. Everything looks fantastic overall, and I’m very excited to see the testing videos and completed assembly. It’s incredible to watch this go from an idea to a real machine.

[CLIENT_NAME_001] Burton

value_updates.wiring_plan_retention: retain wiring layout documentation for potential future development

decisions.reason: Retaining documentation of materials used may imply retaining the BOM, but the client does not explicitly identify the BOM and could be requesting a separate materials record.
CAD-file retention does not alter dispensing-path cleanability; the separate sanitation decision in the same message is already represented in this Requirement.
Retaining CAD files does not change the machine's physical service-access behavior; the same-message food-service scope extension is already represented.
The CAD-retention decision does not change the food-contact material standard, which is independently introduced by another clause of the source message.
Documentation retention does not alter the required separation of liquids from electrical components; the food-service context change is already represented.
Retaining CAD files does not change whisk-removal behavior; the separate retail food-service scope extension from the same message is already represented.
The CAD-file retention decision has no necessary effect on structural rigidity or vibration-control requirements.
The source decision concerns documentation retention and does not modify control placement or control-panel layout.
Retaining CAD documentation does not change the strategy of using off-the-shelf electrical components for the initial prototype.
The documentation-retention decision does not change the prototype's standard 120V wall-power requirement.
Retaining CAD files does not change the required mixing quality, foam outcome, whisk positioning, or high-speed mixing behavior.
